title: Self-coefficient Ext is the conormal-dual exterior sheaf
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], C=i*ker(i) [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback], and V⊆Z open. Suppose every z∈V has an affine neighbourhood of i(z) on which ker(i) is generated by some finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put B=i_*O_Z and G^n=H^n(RHom_Y(B,B)) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every n∈ℕ there exists an isomorphism (i*G^n)|V ≅ exteriorSheaf(Hom(C,O_Z)|V,n) [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. No constant-rank hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 48.15.4, self Ext algebra; Tag 0BQW, intrinsic degree-one comparison

proof.text: On the affine chart A=Γ(Y,U), I=ker(i)(U), B=A/I, take the actual finite free Koszul projective resolution of B and its quotient augmentation. Sheafify using the closed immersion quotient-spectrum identification. The exterior basis makes this a bounded finite free complex.

Restrict derived internal Hom and use the bounded finite free model to identify its natural coefficient morphisms with those of the sheafified Hom complex. The common K-injective model compares the supplied derived universe.

Hom(K,B) has zero differentials since every f_j acts as zero on B. The conormal basis identifies degree-one contractions with Hom_B(I/I²,B). Products of contractions give the nth exterior power in every degree, including n=0 and n exceeding the local length. Affine conormal frames and finite free sheaf Hom and exterior formulas identify the resulting sheaf with the stated target.

The degree-one boundary of the second-order thickening 0→I/I²→O_Y/I²→i_*O_Z→0 is intrinsic, and its alternating Yoneda products define the exterior comparison. A change of generators acts by the dual conormal matrix on contractions and its nth exterior power on products; localization preserves the formulas. Thus the affine comparisons and their inverses agree on standard affine refinements of overlaps and glue on V. No quasi-separatedness is required. Tensor pullback after cohomology leaves the quotient-module action unchanged. Empty V is vacuous.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulRegularImmersion_self_ext_exterior
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (V : Z.Opens) (n : ℕ)
    (hregular : ∀ z : Z, z ∈ V → ∃ U : Y.affineOpens, i z ∈ U.1 ∧
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
        Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G) ≅
      Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf
        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
          (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := Z.sheaf)
            ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules)
            (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf))) n)
